survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD country note summarises system-level indicators for Mexico using the latest available data from Education at a Glance 2025. It does not provide an analyst-facing microdata workflow (e.g., student-level sampling weights, replicate weights, or PV estimation procedures) because it is a descriptive reporting document rather than an empirical student-level modelling study. The note points readers to the corresponding tables and to Education at a Glance 2025: Sources, Methodologies and Technical Notes for indicator-specific collection and processing methods. For any secondary analysis using the underlying OECD datasets, analysts should follow the indicator technical notes to apply the appropriate complex survey design and weighting conventions for the specific source dataset.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a descriptive country note reporting education-system indicators (e.g., attainment, unemployment by education level, expenditure per student, instruction time) rather than estimating cognitive achievement outcomes with PV-based scoring. As a result, plausible values handling is not applicable because no PV-based achievement modelling is performed in this note. Missing-data handling is not reported because the note does not describe an analyst-specific estimation procedure; instead, it directs readers to the OECD technical notes that document indicator construction and data processing for each measure.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used OECD Education at a Glance 2025 indicator data for Mexico (latest available year as stated in the note). No student-level analytic sample is defined in the note; it reports system-level statistics and trends, with indicator-specific reference years and methodological details provided in the linked Education at a Glance 2025 tables and technical notes.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Education at a Glance 2025 country note for Mexico provides a descriptive overview of key education-system characteristics, with emphasis on tertiary education. It reports indicator trends and cross-sectional comparisons such as unemployment rates by educational attainment among 25–34 year-olds, employment and wage gaps by attainment, participation and progression into tertiary education, international student mobility, and government expenditure per student by education level. The note does not conduct student-level modelling, does not specify an analytic ML pipeline, and does not define a microdata sampling frame or PV-based achievement estimation. Instead, it points readers to the corresponding Education at a Glance 2025 tables and to the Sources, Methodologies and Technical Notes for indicator-specific data collection, processing, and any weighting/scaling conventions. Therefore, the document’s “results” are descriptive benchmarks rather than model-based effects, and policy interpretation should rely on the indicator definitions and methodological notes.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is not an empirical large-scale assessment modelling paper; it is a descriptive OECD country note that summarises system-level indicators. Consequently, there is no student-level dataset, no ML model training/evaluation, no PV estimation, and no reported analytic sample size or weighting variables within the note itself. The note’s methodological transparency is deferred to the linked OECD technical notes and indicator tables, which document how each indicator is constructed from underlying data sources.
